result.title: How Robust Are Prognostic Radiomic Features? Comparing Selection Techniques on Pooled Glioblastoma Cohorts
result.summary: Radiomic survival studies in glioblastoma report heterogeneous prognostic features, but how much of this stems from the methodology itself is rarely examined. We analysed the association of 463 radiomic, anatomical and clinical features from pre-treatment MRI with overall survival in 705 IDH-wildtype glioblastoma patients from three public cohorts, using three techniques: a log-rank test after median split, univariate Cox regression (both Benjamini-Hochberg corrected) and an XGBoost regressor interpreted with SHAP. The log-rank test selected 99 features, Cox regression 72 and SHAP its top 20; five were selected by all three: age, a peritumoural T2 texture feature, the number of connected peritumoural mask components and two image-level intensity maxima. The two survival tests shared 51 features, about half of the SHAP top 20 were also selected by either test, and where selections overlapped, effect directions agreed. Many selections were PyRadiomics diagnostic descriptors that are not restricted to tumour voxels. Analytical pipeline choices, including ranking method, pre-filtering and descriptor handling, can substantially influence which features appear prognostic.

AI.brief_summary: 该文比较三种特征选择方法（log-rank、单变量 Cox、SHAP 解释的 XGBoost）在 705 例胶质母细胞瘤患者 MRI 影像组学特征与总生存关联中的选择一致性。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于医学影像组学预后建模的可复现性问题，既无 latent 推理状态、也无视觉证据筛选或 VLM 推理机制，与研究主线的状态表示、生成与决策问题缺少实质联系，也未提供可迁移的方法线索。
